hook: Bethel A.M.E. Church, whose congregation met in a refitted Scott Street carpenter shop before buying on Powell Street in 1862.

parcel.note: The roll classes 916 Laguna Street, a separate parcel (0770015) immediately north and built in 1973, as church property too. SF Heritage describes the Bethel A.M.E. Church as 916–970 Laguna Street, constructed 1969–1973. Which building holds the sanctuary is not established here; the congregation gives its address as 970 Laguna.

historic_status.reason: Historic Survey Result and 45 years or older

permit_summary.note: DBI holds no permit records for this parcel, by block and lot or by street number.

historical_record.description: The Bethel A.M.E. Church buildings at 916–970 Laguna Street were constructed.
The congregation bought a frame building on Powell Street between Jackson and Pacific for $5,500, and met on that site until the 1940s.
The congregation held supper-dances at Assembly Hall, at Post and Kearny Streets — supper with the clergy, dancing after they left.

historical_record.summary: A carpenter shop on Scott Street
historical_record.description: The Reverend Thomas M. D. Ward moved his congregation into a carpenter shop on Scott Street, refitted for religious services, until he could buy a larger building on Powell Street.

narrative.lead: Bethel A.M.E. Church occupies two adjoining parcels, 970 and 916 Laguna Street. This page covers 970, the address the congregation uses.

unknowns: Which of the two church parcels — 970 Laguna Street or 916 Laguna Street — holds the sanctuary, and how the congregation uses each.
The date of the last recorded sale.
Where the congregation met between the 1940s, when it left Powell Street, and 1969.
